answer.answer_markdown:
**(a)** \(120\text{ euros}\times100\text{ yen/euro}=12{,}000\text{ yen}.\)

**(b)** Net financial capital flows toward Japan from Italy increase: higher Japanese real interest rates attract investment, so investors demand yen to purchase Japanese financial assets.

**(c)** The yen market’s demand shifts right (supply unchanged), raising the yen’s value. The vertical axis is the yen’s exchange value in euros per yen; the horizontal axis is quantity of yen.

**(d)** Italy’s exports to Japan decrease. The yen appreciates relative to the euro, so Italian goods become more expensive to Japanese buyers (equivalently, each yen buys more euros, requiring more yen to pay for a euro-priced Italian coat).
